Employees are around 700-1,000. Crunchbase shows about $939 million in funding in August 2026. B2B energy company with limited consumer awareness.

about: Acciona Energia is a Spanish renewable energy company based in Madrid, developing, building and operating wind, solar, hydro and storage assets in Spain, the US, Mexico, Chile, Australia and elsewhere, with about 13-14 GW of installed capacity. It sells electricity to utilities, industrial customers and retail consumers. Acciona SA holds about 80 percent, and the shares are listed on the Spanish stock exchange (ANE) since 2021. Acciona group sponsors sport events, but Acciona Energia itself has limited consumer awareness.

Atome Energy is a UK-headquartered developer of low-carbon fertilizer and green hydrogen projects, based in Leeds, with its flagship Villeta project in Paraguay planned to produce ammonia and nitrate fertilizer using renewable hydroelectric power. Customers would be agricultural fertilizer buyers and industrial users. It has no significant revenue yet and is listed (formerly as Atome Plc on the London AIM market). Crunchbase shows about $867 million in funding, latest in April 2026. B2B project developer, no consumer visibility.

about: Clearway Energy is a US owner of contracted renewable and conventional power assets, based in Princeton, New Jersey, with about 12 GW of wind, solar, storage and thermal capacity and thermal steam and chilled water systems. It sells electricity under long-term contracts to utilities and corporate offtakers. It is sponsored by TotalEnergies and Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) and listed on the NYSE (CWEN, CWEN.A). B2B yieldco with no consumer brand profile.

Radial Power is a Houston, Texas company in the Environmental Consulting sector that provides distributed energy and related services, according to Crunchbase, with $660 million in funding shown for January 2026. The input does not tell what technology it uses, who its customers are or how large it is. The size of the funding figure suggests a project-finance commitment. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Chart Industries is a US industrial gas equipment maker, with a Crunchbase location of Ball Ground, Georgia (Atlanta area), designing and manufacturing process equipment for cryogenic gas handling, such as storage tanks, heat exchangers, LNG liquefaction equipment, hydrogen and carbon capture systems. Customers are energy, industrial gas and chemical firms. It was listed on the NYSE (GTLS), and in 2025 Baker Hughes agreed to acquire it for about $13.6 billion. B2B industrial brand, with no consumer awareness.

Igua Saneamento is a Brazilian water and sewage company, based in Sao Paulo, operating concessions and public-private partnerships that supply drinking water and wastewater treatment to millions of people in cities across several Brazilian states. It was established through investments by Canadian pension capital and other investors. Funding of about $1.3B was recorded in 2024, including debt. Customers are municipalities and households under concession contracts. Regional utility brand with little national consumer awareness.

about: Northumbrian Water is the water and sewerage company for much of north east England, based in Durham, and also supplies water in Essex and Suffolk under the Essex & Suffolk Water brand. It serves millions of customers and has been owned by CK Infrastructure Holdings, the Li Ka-shing group, since 2011. Customers are households and businesses, regulated by Ofwat. Funding of about 877M was recorded in 2024. Regional utility brand, though water companies face criticism over sewage discharges.

Premier Energy is a Romanian and Moldovan energy company, based in Bucharest, that supplies and distributes electricity and gas, operates renewable assets and offers energy solutions to households and businesses. It is the main electricity distributor in Moldova and has grown through acquisitions, backed by private investors. Funding of about EUR 916M was recorded in 2026, partly debt. Utility brand known to customers in Moldova and Romania, with limited recognition elsewhere.

about: Saipem is an Italian oil and gas services group based in Milan, listed on Euronext Milan (SPM) with Eni as a main shareholder. It is a contractor that designs, builds and installs offshore and onshore pipelines, platforms, floating production units, drilling services and carbon capture projects for energy companies and governments in dozens of countries. In 2025 it agreed to merge with Subsea7. Funding of about EUR 893M was recorded in 2024. B2B engineering brand with little consumer awareness.

Seche Environnement is a French environmental services company based in Change, Mayenne, listed on Euronext Paris (SCHP) and controlled by the Seche family group. It handles hazardous and non-hazardous waste treatment, recycling, and decontamination for industry and local authorities in France and international markets such as Latin America and Asia. Revenue is around EUR 1B. Funding of about EUR 770M was recorded in 2025. B2B environmental brand with limited consumer visibility.

Shenzhen Energy Environmental Protection is a Chinese waste-to-energy and environmental services subsidiary of the state-owned Shenzhen Energy Group, based in Shenzhen, Guangdong, building and operating waste incineration power plants and related solid waste treatment facilities across China. It sells electricity and waste treatment services to local governments. Funding of about CN¥5B was recorded in 2025. B2B and government-linked operator with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Chestnut Carbon is a New York developer of large-scale reforestation projects that sell carbon removal credits, planting trees on former agricultural land in the southern United States to remove CO2 and manage them for decades. Its offtake customers include Microsoft, and it has raised financing of about $660M, including a major investment in 2025. Founded in 2021. Customers are corporate buyers of carbon credits. B2B climate brand known in sustainability circles, with little consumer awareness.

about: Polarcus was a Dubai-based marine geophysical company that operated 3D seismic survey vessels to map oil and gas reserves offshore, selling data and services to energy companies, and listed on Oslo Bors. It struggled with the oil downturn, went through creditor restructurings, and wound down its fleet in the early 2020s. Funding of about $610M was recorded in 2025 per the data, which probably reflects older or restructuring financing. B2B oil services brand with no consumer awareness, and likely no longer an active sponsor.
cb_desc: Polarcus is an innovative marine geophysical company.

It looks like a B2B engineering supplier with no consumer brand visibility. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises is an Akron, Ohio, American energy technology and services company that makes boilers, steam generation equipment, environmental systems for emissions control and renewable and waste-to-energy plants, plus aftermarket services for power and industrial customers. Customers are utilities, industrial plants and governments worldwide. Listed on the NYSE (BW), it has revenue of several hundred million dollars, and its roots go back to 1867. It has been working on carbon capture and clean hydrogen technologies. A B2B industrial brand with limited consumer awareness.

Svante is a Burnaby, British Columbia, cleantech company that develops solid sorbent carbon capture filters (using metal-organic frameworks) and builds modular systems that capture CO2 from cement, steel, hydrogen and power plants. Customers are industrial emitters, and it earns revenue from equipment, filters and technology licences, backed by large investors including Chevron and Temasek. Crunchbase shows about $510 million in funding. Privately held, founded in 2007 as Inventys. B2B climate-technology brand with limited consumer visibility, though it features in industrial decarbonisation discussions.

Greenalia is a Spanish renewable energy company based in A Coruna, Galicia, developing and operating wind, solar and biomass power plants in Spain, Portugal, the US and Poland, and acting as an independent power producer. Customers are electricity buyers under power purchase agreements and the grid. Founded in 2011, it listed on the Spanish BME Growth market and continues to expand its pipeline. Crunchbase shows about $430 million in funding. Regional energy brand in northwest Spain, with limited consumer awareness.

Footprint is an Arizona-based materials science company that makes plant-based, molded-fiber packaging as a replacement for plastic, including food service containers, and pursues sustainable food packaging for retailers and brands. It has raised well over 1 billion dollars, including backing from SoftBank Vision Fund, at a valuation reported near 1.7 billion dollars, though it later faced restructuring. Customers are restaurants, consumer goods brands and retailers. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Severn Trent is the UK water utility serving about 4.6 million households and businesses across the Midlands and mid Wales, providing drinking water and sewerage services. It also runs a business services and green power division. Headquartered in Coventry and listed on the London Stock Exchange (SVT) and FTSE 100, with revenue of roughly 2.5 billion pounds. Regulated by Ofwat. Customers know the brand as a local water supplier. Sponsors regional community and sports events.

Energean is an independent oil and gas exploration and production company, headquartered in London, with main operations in Israel (Karish, Tanin and Katlan gas fields via the Energean Power FPSO), plus assets in Egypt, Italy, Croatia and Greece. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (ENOG) and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Customers are Israeli power producers and industrial users under long-term gas contracts. Revenue is roughly 1.5 to 2 billion dollars. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

QazaqGaz is Kazakhstan's state-owned national gas company, based in Astana, which operates gas transmission pipelines, gas processing, storage, domestic supply and exports, and is expanding gas processing and LNG-related projects. It is wholly owned by the sovereign fund Samruk-Kazyna. Customers are households, industry and export buyers. Funding of about 700 million dollars recorded. B2B state energy firm with some domestic consumer exposure through gas supply.

about: Montrose Environmental Group is a US environmental services firm offering testing and analysis, remediation, air quality, water treatment and scientific consulting to industrial, utility and government clients. Crunchbase lists Little Rock, Arkansas as its location. Listed on the NYSE (MEG) since 2020, with revenue of roughly 700 million dollars. Funding of about 670 million dollars. B2B services with no consumer brand.

about: Aris Water Solutions is a Houston-based provider of produced water handling and recycling for oil and gas producers, mainly in the Permian Basin. It owns pipelines, treatment and reuse facilities and sells water services to producers under long-term contracts, with some recycled water supply. Listed on the NYSE (ARIS) since 2021, with revenue around 400 million dollars. Funding around 500 million dollars. B2B energy services with no consumer brand.

HTEC Hydrogen Technology and Energy Corporation is a privately held Vancouver-based company that produces, distributes and dispenses clean hydrogen for fuel cell vehicles, with a network of retail hydrogen stations in British Columbia and the US West Coast. Backed by about 625 million Canadian dollars of funding recorded. Customers are fleet operators, transit companies and drivers of fuel cell cars. Visible niche brand at hydrogen refuelling stations.

Key Capture Energy is a US developer, owner and operator of utility-scale battery energy storage, based in Albany, New York. It builds grid batteries in New York, Texas and other regions, selling capacity and grid services to utilities and grid operators. SK E&S, part of South Korea's SK Group, acquired it in 2021 and later renamed its US platform. It had raised about 300 million dollars. B2B energy developer with no consumer brand profile.

about: Tejon Treating and Carbon Solutions is a US energy services company based in Denver, Colorado, that provides sour gas treating and carbon capture and sequestration services to oil and gas producers. It builds and operates facilities that remove hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide from natural gas, mainly in the Permian and other basins, under long-term contracts. It is private equity backed with about 295 million dollars raised. B2B midstream service provider with no consumer visibility.

about: OCP Green Water is a Moroccan subsidiary of the state-controlled phosphate group OCP, based in the El Jadida area, which focuses on alternative water sources such as seawater desalination and wastewater reuse, mainly to supply OCP's industrial sites and neighbouring communities. The input shows funding of MAD 6 billion, last dated April 2025. It is an industrial utility with no consumer brand awareness.

about: UK energy-from-waste operator that burns household and commercial waste that cannot be recycled to generate electricity and heat, running around ten facilities including in Teesside, Kent, Wales and the Midlands. It handles several million tonnes of waste a year and supplies power to the grid. Formerly Wheelabrator Technologies in the UK, it was bought by Macquarie Asset Management in 2018 and renamed enfinium in 2021. Customers are local authorities and waste firms paying gate fees, plus electricity buyers. B2B with low consumer awareness and a sustainability-led brand.

US developer, owner and operator of utility-scale solar and storage projects, once the largest independent solar power producer in the country, with projects in states such as Virginia and North Carolina. Salt Lake City-based sPower sold electricity under long-term contracts to utilities and corporations. It was jointly owned by AES and AIMCo (Alberta Investment Management), and was folded into AES Clean Energy in 2021. B2B with little consumer awareness, though known in renewable energy finance.

Modern Karton is an Istanbul-based company that, according to Crunchbase, manufactures paper and forest products. Its tags suggest a paper and cardboard manufacturer, but the data provided does not confirm its product range, customers, owners or scale. Such firms usually sell paper and packaging board to converters and packaging customers, so it is probably B2B with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Clean energy technology company commercialising the Allam-Fetvedt cycle, a natural gas power process that burns fuel with oxygen and captures nearly all CO2 emissions, aiming to deliver low-cost power with carbon capture. Based in Durham, North Carolina, it went public on the NYSE (NPWR) in 2023 via a SPAC, with backing from Oxy Low Carbon Ventures, Constellation, Baker Hughes and 8 Rivers. It runs a test plant in La Porte, Texas, and plans commercial plants with partners. B2B technology developer with limited consumer awareness.

Carbon capture and sequestration business of Occidental Petroleum, which develops direct air capture plants, geological sequestration hubs and carbon removal credit sales. Its flagship Stratos facility in the Permian Basin of Texas, built with Carbon Engineering technology, is designed to pull up to around 500,000 tonnes of CO2 a year from the air. Customers include airlines, technology firms and other corporations buying carbon removal credits, such as Microsoft, Amazon and Airbus. Houston-based, wholly owned by Occidental (NYSE: OXY). B2B, with growing profile in climate circles.

Swiss solar technology company that originally made production equipment for solar cell and wafer manufacturing, then moved to making its own heterojunction solar cells and modules at plants in Germany and the United States, selling to residential, commercial and utility customers. Based in Thun, it is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (MBTN). After strong losses and the end of its German module production, it filed for insolvency of its German and US subsidiaries in 2025. B2B and installer-focused, with modest consumer awareness.

Minnesota-based environmental services and recycling company, best known for recycling used lead-acid batteries and producing refined lead and plastics for reuse, with an operation in Minnesota and facilities elsewhere in the United States. It serves battery manufacturers, retailers and industrial customers who need to collect and process end-of-life batteries, and earns income from selling reclaimed lead and polypropylene and from service fees. A mid-sized industrial company with a B2B profile and little consumer brand awareness.
